questions.key_step: Differentiate the functional equation in $x$ only, then put $y=x$ so that $f'(1)$ appears.
questions.justification: Functional equations; Differentiation of a functional relation - 5 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above (paper is JEE Main standard, so well below the Advanced anchors).

questions.key_step: Remove the modulus: $e^{-|\ln x|}=x$ for $0<x<1$ and $\frac1x$ for $x\ge1$; only the junction $x=1$ can fail.
questions.justification: Continuity and differentiability of a composite of modulus and logarithm - 6 steps in the printed solution; level 1 set from the key step above (paper is JEE Main standard, so well below the Advanced anchors).

questions.key_step: Build the graph in stages: $y=2x^2+5x-3$, then $y=2x^2+5|x|-3$, then take the modulus; count the sharp corners.
questions.justification: Continuity and differentiability of modulus functions - 6 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above (paper is JEE Main standard, so well below the Advanced anchors).

questions.key_step: For $|x|<1$ higher powers are closer to $0$, for $|x|>1$ they are farther; so the maximum switches only at $-1,0,1$.
questions.justification: Continuity and differentiability of the maximum of functions - 7 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above (paper is JEE Main standard, so well below the Advanced anchors).

questions.key_step: Each greatest integer function jumps where its inside crosses an integer; jumps that coincide in $f$ at $x=4$ cancel.
questions.justification: Discontinuity of greatest integer functions - 6 steps in the printed solution; level 3 set from the key step above (paper is JEE Main standard, so well below the Advanced anchors).

questions.key_step: Continuity at $0$ means $f(0)=\lim_{x\to0}f(x)$; expand to order $x^3$ since numerator and denominator both start at $x^3$.
questions.justification: Limits using series expansion; Continuity at a point (removable discontinuity) - 6 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above (paper is JEE Main standard, so well below the Advanced anchors).

questions.key_step: On each unit interval $[x]$ is constant, so $f$ is a line; the candidates for trouble are only $x=0,1,2$.
questions.justification: Continuity and differentiability of piecewise functions with greatest integer - 7 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above (paper is JEE Main standard, so well below the Advanced anchors).

questions.key_step: Remove the integer $3$ from the floor, locate the jumps of $\left[\frac x2\right]$ and $[\sqrt x]$, and check the common point $x=4$.
questions.justification: Discontinuity of greatest integer functions - 7 steps in the printed solution; level 3 set from the key step above (paper is JEE Main standard, so well below the Advanced anchors).

questions.key_step: Continuity gives LHL $=f\left(\frac\pi2\right)=$ RHL; the left exponent tends to $0$ and the right limit is a $1^\infty$ form giving $e^{b/a}$.
questions.justification: Continuity at a point; Limits of the $1^\infty$ form and trigonometric limits - 6 steps in the printed solution; level 3 set from the key step above (paper is JEE Main standard, so well below the Advanced anchors).

questions.key_step: Divide by $x-y$ and let $y\to x$ from each side: the two one-sided inequalities squeeze $f'(x)=\frac1x+1$.
questions.justification: Derivative from a functional inequality; Sum of squares of natural numbers - 8 steps in the printed solution; level 3 set from the key step above (paper is JEE Main standard, so well below the Advanced anchors).

questions.key_step: Collect $f(2x+2y)$ and $f(2x-2y)$: the coefficients become $\sin(x-y)$ and $\sin(x+y)$, which separates the variables.
questions.justification: Functional equations with trigonometric factors; Second derivative - 8 steps in the printed solution; level 3 set from the key step above (paper is JEE Main standard, so well below the Advanced anchors).

questions.key_step: $C_3\to C_3-C_1$ kills two entries of the third column, so the determinant collapses to $-(1+\cos x)$.
questions.justification: Properties of determinants (column operations); Successive differentiation - 5 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above (paper is JEE Main standard, so well below the Advanced anchors).

questions.key_step: Differentiate $g(f(x))=x$, then find the $x$ with $f(x)=7$ by inspection: $f(1)=7$.
questions.justification: Derivative of the inverse function - 6 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above (paper is JEE Main standard, so well below the Advanced anchors).

questions.key_step: In terms of $c=\cos\theta$ the denominator factors as $(2c^2+2c-1)(2c+2)$, cancelling the numerator and leaving $\frac1{2(1+\cos\theta)}$.
questions.justification: Multiple-angle trigonometric identities; Successive differentiation - 8 steps in the printed solution; level 3 set from the key step above (paper is JEE Main standard, so well below the Advanced anchors).

questions.key_step: Product rule and chain rule; at $x=0$, $e^0=1$ so only the given values $h(0),h(1),h'(0),h'(1)$ appear.
questions.justification: Chain rule and product rule for composite functions - 4 steps in the printed solution; level 1 set from the key step above (paper is JEE Main standard, so well below the Advanced anchors).

questions.key_step: Three conditions $f(1)$, $f'(1)$, $f''(1)$ give three linear equations; subtracting kills $a$ and shows $b+c=0$.
questions.justification: Higher-order derivatives of a polynomial; Solving linear equations - 6 steps in the printed solution; level 1 set from the key step above (paper is JEE Main standard, so well below the Advanced anchors).

questions.key_step: From $\sqrt{1-x^2}\,y'=3y$, differentiate once more and multiply by $\sqrt{1-x^2}$: the expression equals $9y$.
questions.justification: Successive differentiation (differential relation for an inverse-trigonometric exponent) - 7 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above (paper is JEE Main standard, so well below the Advanced anchors).

questions.key_step: Write $f=\tan x\cdot g(x)$: since $\tan 0=0$, the product rule leaves $f'(0)=g(0)$.
questions.justification: Differentiation of product and quotient functions - 5 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above (paper is JEE Main standard, so well below the Advanced anchors).

questions.key_step: Differentiate the logarithm to get $y'=\frac{-4x}{1-x^4}$, then use the quotient rule once more and evaluate with $x^4=\frac1{16}$.
questions.justification: Successive differentiation of a logarithmic function - 7 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above (paper is JEE Main standard, so well below the Advanced anchors).

questions.key_step: Differentiate the determinant one column at a time; at $x=0$ each differentiated column is zero.
questions.justification: Differentiation of a determinant - 7 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above (paper is JEE Main standard, so well below the Advanced anchors).
